summary: Fort Logan National Cemetery is a United States National Cemetery located in Denver, Colorado. The note says it is named after Union General John A. Logan, who commanded US Volunteer forces during the American Civil War. It had over 122,000 interments as of 2014 and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2016.
one_line: Fort Logan National Cemetery is a U.S. National Cemetery in Denver, Colorado, named for Union General John A. Logan and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2016.
